item.title: Strategic Bitcoin Reserve Bill Clears House Committee, Heads to Floor
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Strategic Bitcoin Reserve Bill Clears House Committee, Heads to Floor A bill that would write the U.S. Strategic Bitcoin Reserve into federal law is now eligible for a vote on the House floor, after the House Financial Services Committee formally reported it on Tuesday. The American Reserve Modernization Act of 2026, H.R. 8957, was filed with amendments as House Report 119-894 and placed on the Union Calendar as Calendar No. 789 on Nov. 24, according to congressional records. The committee had voted 28-21 to advance the bill at a Sept. 16 markup. Rep. Nick Begich, an Alaska Republican, introduced the bill on May 21. It now lists 23 cosponsors, including Rep. Jared Golden, a Maine Democrat, with Reps. Byron Donalds and Maria Elvira Salazar of Florida added on Nov. 24. What the amended bill does The reported text directs the Treasury secretary to set up a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and a separate Digital Asset Stockpile within 180 days of the law taking effect. Bitcoin owned by the federal government would move into the reserve, while other digital assets would go to the stockpile. The centerpiece is a lock-up. Treasury would have to hold all bitcoin deposited in the reserve for at least 20 years after enactment, and during that period no reserve bitcoin could be “sold, swapped, auctioned, encumbered, or otherwise disposed of for any purpose.” After the 20 years, the Treasury secretary could recommend selling up to 10% of the reserve in any two-year period. Two years before the holding period ends, Treasury would have to send Congress recommendations on whether to keep holding or begin a gradual release. Federal agencies would have 60 days after enactment to give Treasury a full accounting of the bitcoin and other digital assets they hold or have seized. Until the reserve is set up, agencies could not sell those coins except for national security, when required by law or a court, or to return assets to crime victims. The bill also creates a Proof of Reserve system. Treasury would publish an annual report on total holdings, transactions and control of private keys, checked by an independent auditor with expertise in cryptographic attestations, while the Government Accountability Office would provide oversight. States could choose to store their own bitcoin in segregated accounts inside the federal reserve, keeping title to the coins and the right to withdraw them. Changes from Begich’s original version The committee rewrote the bill before reporting it. Begich’s introduced text asked Treasury and Commerce to study funding bitcoin purchases with surplus remittances from Federal Reserve Banks or a revaluation of the Fed’s gold certificates, as well as with tax payments, tariff revenue and gifts. Those options are gone from the amended study, which now looks at swapping other digital assets in the stockpile, forfeitures and settlements, and partnerships with states or private entities. item.title: Switzerland Picks 57 Countries for Crypto Tax Data Sharing Starting in 2028
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Switzerland Picks 57 Countries for Crypto Tax Data Sharing Starting in 2028 Switzerland’s Federal Council has approved 57 countries and territories with which the country plans to automatically share tax information on crypto users starting in 2028, extending its long-standing bank data exchange to bitcoin and other digital assets. The list includes all European Union member states, the United Kingdom and various G20 countries, the State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF) said in a release on Wednesday. The exchange will run under the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development’s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework, known as CARF. With the decision, Switzerland intends to implement the crypto exchange at the same time as other global asset management centers, according to the release. The government did not name the 57 jurisdictions beyond those broad groups, and it did not publish the full list alongside the announcement. Exchanges only with partners that qualify Data will not flow to every name on the list. An exchange will take place only if a partner jurisdiction wants to swap information with Switzerland and meets the conditions of the OECD standard, in particular its requirements on confidentiality and data security. Before any financial account or crypto data changes hands, the Federal Council will run a targeted check of whether each partner complies with OECD standards. It will rely on a review mechanism Parliament approved on Sept. 28, 2026, which covers both the older exchange of bank account data and the new crypto exchange. The domestic legal basis for the crypto exchange took effect on Jan. 1, 2026. Earlier this month, though, the SIF said the framework could not be implemented before Jan. 1, 2027, because the partner list still needed approval and notifications had to go to the OECD. The rules do not apply this year. The Council also approved Armenia and Rwanda as new partners for the exchange of financial account information, with first exchanges due in 2028, and signed off on two notifications needed to carry out the exchange. Both partner lists were broadly supported during public consultations in 2024 and 2025, the government said. Down from 74 partners The final list is shorter than first planned. In June 2025, the Federal Council proposed 74 countries relevant to the crypto market, including all EU states, the UK and most G20 members. That plan left out the United States and Saudi Arabia, and it targeted a 2026 start with first data exchanges in 2027. Wednesday’s release did not say which countries were dropped or whether the U.S. is now on the list. The U.S. has committed to begin CARF exchanges by 2029, according to the OECD’s Global Forum, which lists Switzerland among 27 jurisdictions aiming for first exchanges by 2028. item.title: Bithumb Says October Hack Exposed Passports, Bank Accounts and Wallet Addresses
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bithumb Says October Hack Exposed Passports, Bank Accounts and Wallet Addresses South Korean crypto exchange Bithumb said Wednesday that an October hack of its internal systems exposed more people and far more personal data than it first disclosed, including passport numbers, bank account numbers and crypto wallet addresses. The exchange also said the intruder had access for about 15 days before being shut out, not the roughly one hour it reported last month. In an updated notice posted Nov. 25, Bithumb said a follow-up review of the breach of Daou Office, its internal mobile groupware system, turned up additional affected people and additional types of data. The company said the new findings stem from the same incident it disclosed on Oct. 29. Bithumb breach ran for 15 days Bithumb now says an unauthorized outside party accessed the groupware system from 1:49 p.m. on Oct. 12 to 3:22 p.m. on Oct. 27, Korea time, and took personal information and files stored there. That is a sharp change from its first account. Bithumb had said the hack lasted about an hour, from 11:28 a.m. to 12:27 p.m. on Oct. 27, and that it detected the intrusion at 12:14 p.m. that day. The revised timeline means the attacker went unnoticed for more than two weeks. Bithumb first reported that the data of 6,444 customers and 715 employees, or 7,159 people in total, had been exposed. It did not give an updated count on Wednesday. The notice lists customers, employees of partner companies and current and former staff among those affected. Passports, bank accounts and wallet addresses The list of exposed data now runs to 19 items. It includes member numbers, names, mobile numbers, email addresses, dates of birth, resident registration numbers, passport numbers and driver’s license numbers. It also covers bank account numbers, home addresses, gender, nationality, copies of ID documents, occupations, employer names and work contact details, as well as transaction histories and wallet addresses. Bithumb said not every item applies to every person, and that affected users will be told individually by email and text message what was taken. For crypto users, the wallet addresses and transaction records stand out. Paired with names and phone numbers, that kind of data can help scammers target people they know hold digital assets. Bithumb said Daou Office is an internal business system separate from customer exchange accounts and asset data. It said it has found no sign that its exchange service systems or customer database were directly breached, and that it has stepped up real-time monitoring of unusual trades and withdrawals. Bithumb promises compensation The exchange said it blocked the attacker’s IP addresses, fixed the vulnerability behind the incident and is running a security review of all of its externally exposed services. item.title: DOJ Targets 800 Defendants in Largest-Ever Scam Crackdown, Including Crypto Fraud
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine DOJ Targets 800 Defendants in Largest-Ever Scam Crackdown, Including Crypto Fraud The U.S. Justice Department said Tuesday that its largest-ever crackdown on scammers has produced actions against more than 800 defendants since March, with cryptocurrency investment fraud run out of Southeast Asian scam centers among its top targets. The department announced the results of an anti-scam surge that followed President Donald Trump’s Executive Order 14390, signed March 6. Since then, prosecutors have acted in more than 400 cases, bringing new charges, extraditions, guilty verdicts and sentences across 85 federal districts. U.S. agents also helped police in more than 10 countries raid foreign scam call centers and compounds that targeted Americans. Thirty defendants were extradited to face charges in U.S. courts. “Predatory scams against the American people will not be tolerated,” Attorney General Todd Blanche said. “The unprecedented results of this surge are just the beginning.” More than $1 billion in crypto frozen Crypto sits at the center of much of the effort. The State Department said the U.S. and Southeast Asian law enforcement it funds and trains have helped freeze more than $1 billion in stolen cryptocurrency and take down more than 1.4 million fraudulent websites and accounts. The Justice Department’s Scam Center Strike Force, formed in 2025 to go after Southeast Asian crypto fraud, says its crypto seizure team has restrained about $1.08 billion in cryptocurrency from these schemes. The team is focused on returning stolen funds to victims. The FBI’s Operation Blackout has restrained nearly $17 billion in illicit funds, seized more than 14,000 digital devices and helped dismantle more than 29 scam compounds across Asia, Africa and the Middle East, the department said. The FBI also helped free and repatriate more than 2,200 trafficked workers forced to run scams inside those compounds. “The message to these scam syndicates is clear: if you target Americans, justice will find you,” FBI Director Kash Patel said. Scam cases tied to fake crypto platforms In the past month alone, the Criminal Division filed or unsealed charges against more than 30 scam defendants, including those tied to Southeast Asian scam centers running crypto investment fraud schemes. Other cases involved inheritance fraud, jury duty imposters working from Georgia prisons and sweepstakes schemes aimed at elderly Americans. The Secret Service said it has restrained more than $200 million in illicit funds during the surge. One of its cases identified a crypto investment conspiracy run from scam centers in Cambodia that targeted at least 174 U.S. victims. In October, a Chinese national was extradited from the Netherlands and arraigned in California over his alleged role. item.title: HRF Announces Funding of Seven Bitcoin Projects for People Living Under Authoritarian Regimes
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine HRF Announces Funding of Seven Bitcoin Projects for People Living Under Authoritarian Regimes The Human Rights Foundation (HRF) is pleased to announce grants from its Bitcoin Development Fund for seven projects advancing bitcoin self-custody, financial privacy, and education for people living under authoritarian regimes. One project translates bitcoin terminology into 21 African languages. Another mines bitcoin with surplus solar power in rural Nigerian homes, paying it directly to the households that generate it. Others build tools for people facing repression anywhere — activists who need to find and fix the privacy leaks in their bitcoin use, communities who need self-custody devices built from parts found in any electronics store, observers who need election evidence preserved before it disappears, and people who need to turn an ordinary phone into an offline Bitcoin wallet. Together, these efforts help human rights defenders, journalists, nonprofits, and individuals hold, send, and verify their money freely under repression. HRF’s grantees for Round III of 2026 are: CryoBrick Many people want to self-custody bitcoin, but in much of the world, buying a hardware wallet is too expensive. CryoBrick transforms feature phones into offline Bitcoin signing devices. Because it looks and works like an ordinary phone, activists living under authoritarian regimes can self-custody bitcoin while maintaining plausible deniability. Technical Director Apalok will use HRF’s support to conduct comprehensive security hardening and peer review, integrate Bitchat for offline messaging, and publish how-to guides, expanding access to bitcoin and the property rights it protects to a far larger global user base. Exonumia Africa: Bitcoin Glossary Bitcoin’s benefits remain out of reach for many African communities because high-quality education resources do not exist in their local languages. Exonumia , an open-source project that translates Bitcoin educational content, is building a Bitcoin Glossary in 21 African languages. The project will coordinate a continent-wide community of translators through three in-person and 12 virtual translation sprints, where native speakers review and validate more than 250 terms. Because every term is validated by native speakers rather than machines, the approved terms give wallet developers a trustworthy foundation for localizing bitcoin software into African languages, extending access to bitcoin education and the financial freedom it offers. HRF’s support will see the glossary published as a free public resource. Pawavox In much of Africa, democratic elections remain a struggle and most countries are not fully free. Exacerbating this, evidence of fraud documented by citizens is often lost because paper forms go missing and photos and messages cannot be verified. item.title: CleanSpark Weighs Selling More Bitcoin Than It Mines After $987M Loss
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine CleanSpark Weighs Selling More Bitcoin Than It Mines After $987M Loss CleanSpark (Nasdaq: CLSK) may sell more bitcoin than it mines as it works to lower risk on its balance sheet, President and CFO Gary Vecchiarelli said Tuesday, after the miner posted a $987.1 million net loss for its fiscal year ended Sept. 30, as lower bitcoin prices hit the value of its holdings. “We see the selling of a small amount of bitcoin in excess of the quarterly production to be one way of derisking,” Vecchiarelli said on the company’s earnings call. He added that CleanSpark will be “very reactionary to markets” and use that cash to avoid dilution or new debt. Vecchiarelli said CleanSpark already aims to sell virtually all of the bitcoin it mines to run the business, and that it has sold some bitcoin since year-end to build cash for acquisitions it expects to make soon. “It is reasonable to expect that we will fund highly accretive acquisitions and development of projects by selling or borrowing against our bitcoin,” he said. Bitcoin swings drove the loss The Las Vegas-based company reported full-year revenue of $576.5 million, down 25%. The loss came to $3.74 per basic share, and adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $304.2 million. Vecchiarelli said about two-thirds of the swing from last year’s $364 million profit came from noncash mark-to-market losses on bitcoin. CleanSpark recorded a $281.6 million loss on the fair value of its bitcoin for the year, versus a $425.6 million gain a year earlier. It also took $177.1 million in impairment charges, mostly tied to turning its Sandersville, Georgia, mining site into a data center. Bitcoin ended the fiscal year near $83,600, down from about $114,000, the CFO said. The fourth quarter looked different. CleanSpark earned $9.8 million, or 4 cents a share, helped by a $305.6 million gain on its bitcoin, even as revenue dropped 46% from a year earlier to $120.9 million. Analysts had expected a loss of 33 cents a share and revenue of about $134.3 million, Investing.com reported . The miner produced 7,253 BTC during the year, down 8% as network difficulty rose and it curtailed some machines, and ended September with about 200,000 machines running, down from 225,000 at the end of June. That cut lifted fleet efficiency to 14.8 joules per terahash, while average hashrate fell to 36.0 EH/s. CleanSpark held 13,530 BTC, including pledged collateral, at the end of September, worth about $1.1 billion then. Its annual report shows it sold 1,532 bitcoin during the year and used another 6,068 to settle derivatives. At Wednesday’s price near $57,700, 13,530 BTC would be worth roughly $780 million. CleanSpark shares hit a new low CleanSpark stock fell to a new 52-week low of $4.43 shortly after Wednesday’s open, before trimming losses to about $4.85 around 10 a.m. ET, down roughly 5% from Tuesday’s $5.12 close, as the Nasdaq sank about 4% at the open. item.title: Next Technology (NXTT) Sells 500 Bitcoin to Fund AI Push
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Next Technology (NXTT) Sells 500 Bitcoin to Fund AI Push Next Technology Holding (Nasdaq: NXTT) sold about 500 bitcoin last week and said it will put the money toward artificial intelligence projects, the latest public company to trim its bitcoin treasury as prices slide. The Japan-based software firm disclosed in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Tuesday that it sold the coins on Nov. 21 for about $29.22 million. That works out to an average price of $58,468.11 per bitcoin, net of fees and expenses. The sale leaves NXTT with 5,333 BTC. The company was paid in tether (USDT), the dollar-pegged stablecoin, rather than in dollars. NXTT said it plans to use the proceeds for research and development of its AI-related initiatives, including its AI software products and services, as well as for general corporate purposes. A shift away from buying The sale is the first under a program the company’s board approved on Oct. 30. That program allows NXTT to sell or pledge its bitcoin “from time to time in one or more tranches,” through exchange sales, block trades or loans that use the coins as collateral, with the stated aim of “reducing risk exposure and enhancing liquidity.” The filing also repeats a line from the company’s latest quarterly report that marks a clear break from its earlier approach. NXTT “does not currently expect to purchase additional Bitcoin,” the company said, adding that it has adjusted its strategy to focus on managing the coins it already holds. The program has no expiration date and doesn’t require the company to sell any set amount. The board can change, pause or end it at any time. As of Nov. 24, NXTT said it had not pledged any of its bitcoin as collateral. How NXTT built its stack NXTT, which is incorporated in Wyoming but based in Saitama Prefecture, Japan, describes itself as running two strategies: AI-enabled software development and holding bitcoin. It keeps substantially all of its coins with Japan-based institutional custodians, according to its quarterly filing . The company held 833 BTC at the end of 2024 and added 5,000 BTC in 2025, bringing its total to 5,833 BTC. Its filing puts the cost basis of those coins at about $183.1 million, or roughly $31,400 per bitcoin, meaning last week’s sale still came in well above what the company paid on average. Falling prices have still hit the books. NXTT reported a net loss of $32.2 million for the first nine months of 2026, compared with net income of $295.1 million a year earlier. The company said the swing came mainly from a drop in the fair value of its digital assets. The company has also been reshaping its leadership around AI. Earlier this month it named Chan Phang Chuen, a former platform architect focused on computing infrastructure and AI inference, as chief technical officer after Hongliang Liu resigned from the role. Treasury firms turn sellers NXTT joins a growing list of public companies selling bitcoin to fund other businesses.
